title: Grafana MCP Server
summary: Let your agent search Grafana dashboards, query Prometheus and Loki and read alert rules through Grafana's own MCP server, in read-only mode.
description: The Grafana MCP server connects an agent to a Grafana instance through a service account. It can find dashboards, run PromQL and LogQL queries against your datasources and list alert rules, so you can ask about a metric instead of hunting through panels.
This setup starts it with uvx and passes the --disable-write flag, which blocks every create, update and delete call. Remove the flag only if you want the agent to edit dashboards or alerts.
useWhen: Find the dashboard that tracks checkout latency
Run a Prometheus query for error rate over the last hour
Search Loki logs for a failing request id
See which alert rules are firing right now

mcp.name: grafana

env.name: GRAFANA_URL
env.description: Base URL of your Grafana instance, such as https://myinstance.grafana.net

env.name: GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN
env.description: A Grafana service account token; give the account a Viewer role to match the read-only flag

access: Reads dashboards, datasources, alert rules and query results from your Grafana
Runs queries against Prometheus, Loki and other datasources the token can reach
Cannot change anything while --disable-write is set

example.prompt: Which alert rules in the payments folder are firing, and what does the p95 latency query for the checkout service return for the last 30 minutes?
example.result: Two rules are firing: PaymentsQueueDepth and CheckoutErrorBudget. The p95 latency query shows 410 ms now, up from 180 ms at the start of the window, with the jump at 14:12.

faq.question: Do I need to install Grafana tools first?
faq.answer: Only uv, which provides uvx. The server itself is fetched on first run.

faq.question: Can the agent change my dashboards?
faq.answer: Not with this config. The --disable-write flag removes the tools that create, update or delete. The raw SQL tools are removed too.

faq.question: Does it work with Grafana Cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. Set GRAFANA_URL to your .grafana.net address and use a service account token from that stack.

access: Reads dashboards, alerts and datasource queries
Write tools are turned off by the flag
